about: Skills a person opened and read before they were listed here. A GitHub entry is pinned to the commit that was read (repo, path, commit). A bundled entry ships inside Hoprig (bundled: a folder of this package); its integrity is the installed package and its version is Hoprig's. Signals say when a project needs one: <ecosystem>:<dependency> (npm, pub, pypi, go, cargo), stack:<name>, artifact:<kind>, file:<kind>, or always.

entries.for: Teaches your coding tools to use Hoprig itself: check the setup, providers, limits, computers, projects and skills, read-only first, the user decides changes.

Sets up and builds a new project from its owner's brief, fitted to its kind and size: asks once with recommended answers, writes its documents before code, builds the whole product or the set-up only, then reviews and reports.
Turns a goal into a short research note and a proposed plan with milestones and dated tasks, and creates nothing before a yes; Work's Plan with AI follows it.
Brings the projects a computer already has into the workspace: looks only where the owner says, a plan per project, a proved copy after his yes; never retires an original.
A defensive security audit of a codebase: reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, independent validation, a findings report.
entries.notes: Ships two zero-dependency Node validators (validate-findings.cjs, validate-coverage-ledger.cjs) and their tests; it asks for a sandbox before running any target code.

entries.for: Inspect shipped artefacts you own (APK, IPA, Electron/ASAR, native binaries) with the REA tool: what the built app really contains.
entries.notes: Instructions only; the analysis needs the rea command-line tool (npm package rea-agents), which Hoprig checks and updates separately.

entries.for: React and Next.js performance rules from Vercel Engineering for writing and reviewing components.
React Native and Expo practices: list performance, animations, native modules.
From the Next.js team: audit and cut what the browser loads first (big client bundles, duplicate dependencies).
From the Next.js team: check that a change really works in the running app (next dev's MCP view plus a browser), not only that it compiles.
From the Flutter team: structure a Flutter app in the recommended layers (UI, logic, data).
From the Flutter team: write widget tests with WidgetTester (rendering, taps, scrolling, text input).
From Supabase: Postgres rules for schemas, column types, indexes, queries and connections, for Postgres anywhere.
From Docker: write and review Dockerfiles (multi-stage builds, layer caching, smaller and hardened images).
entries.notes: Includes scripts/verify-build.sh, which builds an image when the agent runs it.

entries.for: From Anthropic: test a local web app with Playwright (check pages, click through, screenshots, browser logs).
entries.notes: Ships Python helper scripts that start your dev server and drive a browser.

entries.for: From Anthropic: deliberate visual design for new or reworked UI (direction, typography, avoiding template looks).
From Anthropic: build good MCP servers (tool design, TypeScript or Python SDK, evaluations).
